statement: The guideline requires the contractor to define the authorized work elements for the program, and records that a product-oriented work breakdown structure tailored for effective internal management control is commonly used for that purpose.
quote: Define the authorized work elements for the program. A product-oriented work breakdown structure, tailored for effective internal management control, is commonly used in this process.

statement: The work breakdown structure is a product-oriented, hierarchical breakdown of the program requirements that includes all program elements, such as hardware, software, services, data or facilities.
quote: The WBS is a product-oriented, hierarchical breakdown of the program requirements. The WBS includes all program elements (e.g., hardware, software, services, data, or facilities)

statement: The work breakdown structure must also include all subcontracted work scope.
quote: The WBS must also include all subcontracted work scope.

statement: The contractor must extend the contract work breakdown structure to a level needed for effective internal management control, and this level should not be an arbitrary level established across the program.
quote: In all cases, the contractor must extend the contract WBS to a level needed for effective internal management control. This should not be an arbitrary level established across the program.

statement: Cost collection requirements, such as cost and software data reporting, may require a different reporting structure than the work breakdown structure used in the earned value management system for program management.
quote: Cost collection requirements, such as Cost and Software Data Reporting (CSDR), may require a different reporting structure other than the WBS used in the Earned Value Management System (EVMS)

statement: A single product-oriented work breakdown structure is used for a given contract and extends to the level necessary for management action, comprising all contract work scope including subcontracted and intercompany scope.
quote: A single product-oriented WBS is used for a given contract and extends to the level necessary for management action. The WBS comprises all contract work scope, including subcontracted and intercompany scope, to levels needed for effective internal management control.

statement: The section opened for this topic is the guide's organization guideline on defining the program organizational breakdown structure, labelled in the source as an EIA standard guideline.
quote: GUIDELINE 2: DEFINE PROGRAM ORGANIZATIONAL BREAKDOWN STRUCTURE EVMS Category: Organization EIA Standard Guideline: 2.1b
note: The printed source is page text from the DoD EVMS Interpretation Guide, so no codified or RFO citation is recorded for it.

statement: The guideline requires the contractor to identify the program organizational structure, including the major subcontractors, responsible for accomplishing the authorized work, and to define the organizational elements where work will be planned and controlled.
quote: Identify the program organizational structure, including the major subcontractors, responsible for accomplishing the authorized work and define the organizational elements where work will be planned and controlled.

statement: The hierarchical alpha-numeric unique coding of the organization structure results in the organizational breakdown structure.
quote: The hierarchical alpha-numeric unique coding of the organization structure results in the Organizational Breakdown Structure (OBS).

statement: When designating the internal organization responsible for managing the program, the contractor must assign a program manager with sufficient authority and responsibility to ensure performance of the authorized work.
quote: When designating the internal organization responsible for managing the program efforts, the contractor must assign a program manager with sufficient authority and responsibility to ensure the performance of the authorized work.

statement: The manager assigned to subcontractor work must have full responsibility for the authorized work.
quote: The manager assigned to subcontractor work must have full responsibility for the authorized work.

statement: A single organizational structure exists that contains all organizational elements defined by the organizational breakdown structure, including major subcontractors and inter-company work, as necessary to execute the contract.
quote: A single organizational structure exists that contains all of the organizational elements as defined by the OBS, including major subcontractors and inter-company work, necessary to execute the contract.

statement: The organizational breakdown structure is defined with uniquely defined nomenclature.
quote: The OBS is defined with uniquely defined nomenclature

statement: The section opened for this topic is the guide's organization guideline on integrating the work breakdown structure and the organizational structure, labelled in the source as an EIA standard guideline.
quote: GUIDELINE 3: INTEGRATE WBS AND OBS TO CREATE CONTROL ACCOUNTS EVMS Category: Organization EIA Standard Guideline: 2.1c
note: The printed source is page text from the DoD EVMS Interpretation Guide, so no codified or RFO citation is recorded for it.

statement: The guideline requires the contractor to integrate the program work breakdown structure and organizational structure to identify management control points where responsibility is assigned to specific work scope.
quote: Integrate the program work breakdown structure and organizational structure to identify management control points where responsibility is assigned to specific work scope.

statement: The intersection of the lowest level work breakdown structure element and the organizational breakdown structure is the point at which control accounts are established.
quote: The intersection of the lowest level WBS element and the OBS is the point at which control account(s) are established.

statement: Control accounts should not be arbitrarily established at a single work breakdown structure level across the program.
quote: Control Accounts should not be arbitrarily established at a single WBS level across the program.

statement: Each control account has a corresponding control account manager, who is responsible for ensuring the accomplishment of work in the control account and is the focal point of management control.
quote: Each control account has a corresponding Control Account Manager (CAM), who is responsible for ensuring the accomplishment of work in the control account and is the focal point of management control.

statement: For management control purposes there may be one or more responsible organizations supporting a single work breakdown structure element, or multiple control accounts within one organizational element, driven by scope and exit criteria.
quote: For management control purposes, there may be one or more responsible organizations supporting a single WBS or multiple control accounts within one OBS element driven by scope and exit criteria

statement: For scope that cannot practically be identified to a control account, it is permissible to establish a summary level planning package above the control account level with an assigned manager.
quote: For scope that cannot practically be identified to a control account, it is permissible to establish a Summary Level Planning Package (SLPP) above the control account level with the assignment of an SLPP manager

statement: Each control account is assigned to a single organizational element directly responsible for the work identifiable to a single element of the work breakdown structure.
quote: Each control account is assigned to a single organizational element directly responsible for the work identifiable to a single element of the WBS.

statement: The section opened for this topic is the guide's organization guideline on integrating subsidiary management processes, labelled in the source as an EIA standard guideline.
quote: GUIDELINE 4: INTEGRATE SUBSIDIARY MANAGEMENT PROCESSES EVMS Category: Organization EIA Standard Guideline: 2.1d
note: The printed source is page text from the DoD EVMS Interpretation Guide, so no codified or RFO citation is recorded for it.

statement: The guideline requires the contractor to provide for the integration of the scheduling, budgeting, work authorization and cost accumulation processes with each other and, as appropriate, with the program work breakdown structure and organizational structure.
quote: Provide for the integration of the scheduling, budgeting, work authorization, and cost accumulation processes with each other and, as appropriate, the program work breakdown structure and organizational structure

statement: Integrating planning, scheduling, budgeting, work authorization and cost accumulation management processes provides the capability for establishing the performance measurement baseline, identifying work progress and collecting actual costs.
quote: The integration of planning, scheduling, budgeting, work authorization, and cost accumulation management processes provides the capability for establishing the Performance Measurement Baseline (PMB), identifying work progress, and collecting actual costs

statement: Through coding structures that use unique identifiers and common data elements, or a simple mapping method, the contractor's planning, scheduling, budgeting, work authorization and cost accumulation processes are integrated.
quote: Through coding structures that use unique identifiers (UIDs) and common data elements or a simple mapping method, the contractor’s planning, scheduling, budgeting, work authorization, and cost accumulation processes are integrated.

statement: The earned value system must integrate subcontractor data.
quote: The system must integrate subcontractor data.

statement: The planning, scheduling, budgeting, work authorization and cost accumulation subsystems are integrated via a common and unique coding structure for all levels of the contract work breakdown structure and the organizational structure.
quote: The planning, scheduling, budgeting, work authorization, and cost accumulation subsystems are integrated via a common and unique coding structure for all levels of the Contract Work Breakdown Structure (CWBS) and the organizational structure.

statement: The fifth earned value guideline directs the contractor to identify in the schedule the physical products, milestones, technical performance goals, or other objective indicators used to measure progress.
quote: Identify, in the schedule, the physical products, milestones, technical performance goals, or other objective indicators that will be used to measure progress.

statement: The guideline ensures that program schedules establish and maintain a relationship between technical achievement and progress statusing, providing objective performance data that accurately reflects the progress of the work.
quote: To ensure program schedule(s) establish and maintain a relationship between technical achievement and progress statusing and provide objective performance data that accurately reflects the progress of the work.

statement: Interim measures are defined as the detailed schedule is established to ensure performance is measured as objectively as possible.
quote: Interim measures are defined as the detailed schedule is established to ensure performance is measured as objectively as possible.

statement: Identifying objective criteria linked to technical progress indicators ensures that performance assessments reflect the true technical performance of the program.
quote: Identifying objective criteria, linked to technical progress indicators, ensures performance assessments reflect the true technical performance of the program.

statement: Objective program milestones aligned with the accomplishment of technical requirements and goals are determined in advance, documented, and used to plan and measure progress.
quote: Objective program milestones aligned with the accomplishment of the program’s technical requirements and goals are determined in advance, documented, and used to plan and measure progress.

statement: The sixth earned value guideline requires scheduling authorized work in a manner that describes the sequence of work and identifies task interdependencies required to meet program requirements.
quote: Schedule the authorized work in a manner that describes the sequence of work and identifies task interdependencies required to meet the requirements of the program.

statement: The Integrated Master Schedule includes a baseline schedule and a forecast schedule.
quote: The IMS includes a baseline and forecast schedule.

statement: The forecast schedule is the basis for the time-phased Estimate to Complete.
quote: The forecast schedule is the basis for the time-phased Estimate to Complete.

statement: When level of effort is included in the Integrated Master Schedule, it will not impact discrete work or the calculation of the critical and driving paths.
quote: In the event Level of Effort (LOE) is included in the IMS, it will not impact discrete work or the calculation of the critical and driving paths.

statement: The prime contractor is responsible for planning and integrating material and subcontracted effort into the prime's Integrated Master Schedule.
quote: The prime contractor is responsible for planning and integrating material and subcontracted effort into the prime’s IMS.

statement: Schedule Visibility Tasks carry no resources and provide management visibility into a timespan that might otherwise be modeled in the Integrated Master Schedule with a lag or constrained milestone.
quote: Schedule Visibility Tasks (SVTs) have no resources and provide management visibility into a timespan that may otherwise be modelled in the IMS with a lag or constrained milestone.

statement: A Schedule Visibility Task is not part of the budgeted program scope in the Performance Measurement Baseline nor used to assess earned value performance.
quote: An SVT is not part of the budgeted program scope in the PMB nor used to assess earned value performance.

statement: Schedule margin, if used, is identifiable, derived from a risk management approach, and justifiable in duration; it may only be represented in the schedule as the last task before key contractual events, significant logical integration/test milestones, end item deliverables, and/or contract completion.
quote: Schedule margin, if used, is identifiable, derived from a risk management approach, justifiable in duration, and may only be represented in the schedule as the last task before key contractual events, significant logical integration/test milestones, end item deliverables, and/or contract completion.

statement: The seventh earned value guideline requires establishing and maintaining a time-phased budget baseline comprised of scope, schedule, and budget at the control account level, although budget for far-term efforts may be held in higher-level accounts until an appropriate time for allocation at the control account level.
quote: Establish and maintain a time-phased budget baseline comprised of scope, schedule, and budget at the control account level. Budget for far-term efforts may be held in higher-level accounts until an appropriate time for allocation at the control account level.

statement: The Performance Measurement Baseline is the time-phased budget plan against which actual performance is assessed.
quote: The PMB is the time-phased budget plan against which actual performance is assessed.

statement: For future effort that cannot practically be identified to a control account, it is permissible to establish a Summary Level Planning Package above the control account level.
quote: For future effort that cannot practically be identified to a control account, it is permissible to establish an SLPP above the control account level.

statement: Budget set aside for known and unforeseen program risks and contingencies is referred to as Management Reserve and is not included in the Performance Measurement Baseline.
quote: The budget set aside for known and unforeseen program risks and contingencies is referred to as Management Reserve (MR) and is not included in the PMB

statement: When Total Allocated Budget exceeds the Contract Budget Base, an Over Target Baseline occurs.
quote: When the Total Allocated Budget (TAB) exceeds the CBB, an Over Target Baseline (OTB) occurs.

statement: When the baseline schedule exceeds contract milestones, an Over Target Schedule occurs.
quote: When the baseline schedule exceeds contract milestones, an Over Target Schedule (OTS) occurs

statement: The Performance Measurement Baseline is time-phased in alignment with the Integrated Master Schedule, with budget distributed in accordance with the accounting calendar for authorized work scope including control accounts and summary level planning packages.
quote: The PMB is time-phased in alignment with the Integrated Master Schedule (IMS), with budget distributed in accordance with the accounting calendar for the authorized work scope including all control accounts and SLPPs.

statement: The eighth earned value guideline requires authorizing control account scope, schedule, and budget comprised of elements of cost, such as labor, material, and subcontractors, required to complete the effort.
quote: Authorize control account scope, schedule, and budget comprised of elements of cost (labor, material, subcontractors, etc.) required to complete the effort.

statement: Approved work authorization precedes the baseline start and actual start of work.
quote: Approved work authorization precedes the baseline start and actual start of work.

statement: Budgets are established by element of cost: direct labor, subcontractor, material, and other direct costs.
quote: Budgets are established by EOC: direct labor, subcontractor, material, and other direct costs

statement: Current rates are to be utilized when incorporating new scope into the Performance Measurement Baseline.
quote: Current rates are to be utilized when incorporating new scope into the PMB.

statement: Descoped work is to be removed using the rates that are baselined with the affected scope.
quote: Descoped work is to be removed using the rates that are baselined with the affected scope

statement: The budget for authorized subcontractor work is based initially on the prime contractor's estimated value.
quote: The budget for authorized subcontractor work is based initially on the prime contractor’s estimated value

statement: The ninth earned value guideline requires planning authorized scope, schedule, and budget into work packages and planning packages.
quote: Plan the authorized scope, schedule, and budget into work packages and/or planning packages.

statement: Budgets are determined in terms of dollars, hours, or other measurable units such that the sum of all work package and planning package budgets equals the control account budget.
quote: Determine budgets in terms of dollars, hours, or other measurable units such that the sum of all work package and planning package budgets equal the control account budget.

statement: Work packages reflect the expected way the work is to be done and are a distinguishable subdivision of a control account, assignable to a single program organizational element.
quote: Work packages reflect the expected way the work is to be done and are a distinguishable subdivision of a control account, assignable to a single program organizational element.

statement: Distributing all control account budgets to either work packages or planning packages ensures the Performance Measurement Baseline is planned at an executable level that aligns with how meaningful performance measurements will be achieved.
quote: Distributing all control account budgets to either work packages or planning packages ensures the Performance Measurement Baseline (PMB) is planned at an executable level that aligns with how meaningful performance measurements will be achieved.

statement: When authorized control account work scope cannot be planned in the near-term, a planning package is used for holding scope, schedule, and budget until the work is detail planned into work packages.
quote: When authorized control account work scope cannot be planned in the near-term, a planning package is used for holding the scope, schedule, and budget until the work is detail planned into work packages.

statement: The planning package is time-phased with known schedule requirements and detail planned into work packages at the earliest practicable point before work is performed on its scope.
quote: The planning package is time-phased with the known schedule requirements and is detail planned into work package(s) at the earliest practicable point before any work is performed on the scope contained in the planning package.

statement: The sum of all work package budgets plus planning package budgets within control accounts equals the budgets authorized for those control accounts.
quote: The sum of all work package budgets plus planning package budgets within control accounts equals the budgets authorized for those control accounts.

statement: The DoD EVMS Interpretation Guide presents this requirement as its tenth guideline, on establishing performance measurement criteria.
quote: 3.6 GUIDELINE 10: ESTABLISH PERFORMANCE MEASUREMENT CRITERIA
note: This is guide text, not a codified FAR, DFARS or CAS section.

statement: An earned value management system establishes objective performance measurement criteria for each work package, consistent with the way the work is expected to be accomplished, and identifies only effort that is not measurable as level of effort.
quote: Establish objective performance measurement criteria for each work package consistent with the way work is expected to be accomplished. Only that effort which is not measurable is identified as level of effort.

statement: Classification of work as level of effort is limited to activities that have no practicable, measurable output or product that can be discretely planned and objectively measured at the work package level.
quote: Classification of work scope as Level of Effort (LOE) is limited to activities that have no practicable, measurable output or product associated with technical effort that can be discretely planned and objectively measured at the work package level.

statement: The control account manager assesses each assigned work package and determines whether there is a discrete way to measure progress towards its completion.
quote: The Control Account Manager assesses each assigned Work Package and determines if there is a discrete way to measure progress towards its completion.

statement: Where long-duration work packages are unavoidable, interim milestones that model measurable technical accomplishment are required for performance measurement.
quote: Where long-duration work packages are unavoidable, interim milestones modelling measurable, technical accomplishment are required for performance measurement.

statement: Apportioned effort should be used when work of a supporting nature ties directly to a discrete technical activity.
quote: The concept of "apportioned effort" should be used when work of a supporting nature ties directly to a discrete technical activity.

statement: If the contractor chooses to use apportioned effort, the system documentation must cover the requirements for the technique and must document the factor used to establish the relationship.
quote: If the contractor chooses to use this technique, the EVMS documentation must cover the requirements for the use of this measurement technique and the need to document the factor used to establish the relationship

statement: Level of effort earned value reflects only the passage of time during which those activities are planned, so it never produces a schedule variance and always equals the budgeted cost for work scheduled.
quote: The nature of LOE is such that the BCWP reflects only the passage of time during which LOE activities are planned; there is never a Schedule Variance (SV) (i.e., BCWP always equals BCWS).

statement: The method that calculates BCWP as (ACWP/EAC) x BAC requires the estimate at completion to be evaluated and updated every month.
quote: BCWP = (ACWP/EAC) x BAC. The use of this method requires that the EAC be evaluated and updated every month.

statement: Earned value for discrete material items may be claimed upon receipt, inspection and acceptance only if the items are placed into use within a reasonable time or are specifically identified to a serially numbered end item.
quote: BCWP for discrete material items may be claimed upon receipt, inspection, and acceptance, provided the material items are placed into use within a reasonable time or are specifically identified to a serially numbered end item.

statement: The DoD EVMS Interpretation Guide presents this requirement as its eleventh guideline, on establishing indirect budgets.
quote: 3.7 GUIDELINE 11: ESTABLISH INDIRECT BUDGETS

statement: Indirect rates developed by the responsible organizations are applied to the program’s direct resource budgets at the applicable level, which determines the indirect budgets that support the establishment of the performance measurement baseline.
quote: Apply indirect rates, developed by the responsible organizations, to the program’s direct resource budgets, at the applicable level, to determine the indirect budgets that support the establishment of the performance measurement baseline.

statement: Indirect budgets such as overhead, general and administrative cost, and cost of money are established and included in the performance measurement baseline at an appropriate level for visibility.
quote: To ensure indirect budgets (e.g., Overhead, General & Administrative, and Cost of Money) are established and included in the Performance Measurement Baseline (PMB) at the appropriate level for visibility.

statement: The guide treats it as critical to the contractor that, at the end of the accounting year, all indirect expenses are allocated.
quote: It is critical to the contractor that, at the end of the accounting year, all indirect expenses are allocated.

statement: Indirect budgets are established at the appropriate organizational level for each pool and cost sub-element.
quote: Indirect budgets are established at the appropriate organizational level for each pool and cost sub-element.

statement: Budgets for indirect costs on programs are developed and planned in conjunction with the direct budgets and are consistent with the contractor’s documented procedures for how indirect costs are approved and allocated to the program.
quote: Budgets for indirect costs as implemented on the programs are developed and planned in conjunction with the direct budgets and are consistent with the contractor’s documented procedures for how indirect costs are approved and allocated to the program

statement: Indirect budgets are incorporated into the baseline in concert with the described processes and current rates, which may be approved, provisional or proposed.
quote: Indirect budgets are incorporated into the PMB in concert with described processes and current rates (i.e., approved, provisional, proposed).

statement: Comparing actual indirect expenses with the established indirect budgets shows whether absorption under the existing documented allocation schemes is on track or whether allocation rates require adjustment.
quote: By comparing actual indirect expenses to established indirect budgets, the contractor can determine if the absorption of indirect expenses based on existing documented allocation schemes is on track or if allocation rates require adjustment.

statement: The DoD EVMS Interpretation Guide presents this requirement as its twelfth guideline, on identifying undistributed budget and management reserve.
quote: 3.8 GUIDELINE 12: IDENTIFY UNDISTRIBUTED BUDGET AND MANAGEMENT RESERVE

statement: Undistributed budget is budget that applies to specific contractual effort that has not yet been distributed to control accounts or summary level planning packages.
quote: UB is budget that applies to specific contractual effort that has not yet been distributed to control accounts or Summary Level Planning Packages (SLPPs).

statement: Undistributed budget accommodates contract situations where authorized scope and budget cannot yet be distributed within the baseline to control accounts or summary level planning packages.
quote: UB accommodates contract situations where authorized scope and budget cannot yet be distributed within the Performance Measurement Baseline (PMB) to control accounts or SLPPs.

statement: Undistributed budget is part of the performance measurement baseline and is budget associated with contractually authorized scope that has not yet been distributed to an organizational element at or below the reporting level.
quote: UB is part of the PMB and is budget associated with contractually authorized work scope that has not yet been distributed to an organizational element at or below the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) reporting level.

statement: Undistributed budget is a transitional budget that should be distributed in a timely manner.
quote: UB is a transitional budget that should be distributed in a timely manner.

statement: Management reserve belongs to the contractor program manager, not the Government, and provides the contractor with a budget for unplanned activities within the current program scope.
quote: MR belongs to the contractor program manager, not the Government, and provides the contractor with a budget for unplanned activities within the current program scope.

statement: Management reserve is not associated with a specific scope of work and is not included in the performance measurement baseline.
quote: MR is not associated with a specific scope of work and is not included in the PMB.

statement: Management reserve is not a contingency fund: it may not be eliminated from contract prices by the customer during later negotiations and may not be used to absorb the cost of contract changes.
quote: MR is not a contingency fund and may neither be eliminated from contract prices by the customer during subsequent negotiations nor used to absorb the cost of contract changes.

statement: Management reserve is always reported as a positive value and is set aside for program risks or unplanned events that are in scope to the contract.
quote: MR is always reported as a positive value and is set aside for program risks or unplanned events that are in-scope to the contract.

statement: Management reserve belonging to a major subcontractor is incorporated into the prime contractor’s earned value system with traceability to the subcontractor’s reported reserve.
quote: MR belonging to a major subcontractor is incorporated into the prime contractor’s EVMS with traceability to the subcontractor’s reported MR.

statement: Undistributed budget has defined scope, is separately identified, is traceable to contractual actions and is part of the baseline, while management reserve has no scope defined and is separately identified outside the baseline.
quote: UB has defined scope, is separately identified, is traceable to contractual actions, and is part of the PMB. MR has no scope defined and is separately identified outside of the PMB.
note: The guide states that undistributed budget and management reserve serve distinctly different purposes.

statement: The DoD EVMS Interpretation Guide presents this requirement as its thirteenth guideline, on reconciling to target costs.
quote: 3.9 GUIDELINE 13: RECONCILE TO TARGET COSTS

statement: The program target cost goal is reconciled with the sum of all internal program budgets and management reserve.
quote: Provide that the program target cost goal is reconciled with the sum of all internal program budgets and management reserve.

statement: Contract target cost is synonymous with negotiated contract cost.
quote: Contract Target Cost is synonymous with Negotiated Contract Cost (NCC).

statement: The contract target cost plus authorized unpriced work must reconcile with the contract budget base and the total allocated budget.
quote: The Contract Target Cost plus Authorized Unpriced Work (AUW) must reconcile with the Contract Budget Base (CBB)/Total Allocated Budget (TAB).

statement: Control account budgets, summary level planning packages and undistributed budget are summed to the budget at completion of the baseline, and that sum plus management reserve equals the contract budget base.
quote: All control account budgets, SLPPs, and UB are summed up to a total value known as the Budget at Completion (BAC) of the PMB. Having validated the sum of the internal budgets, this sum plus MR equals the value known as the CBB.

statement: The contract budget base also equals the total allocated budget unless a recognized over-target baseline exists; with one, the total allocated budget equals the contract budget base plus the above target budget.
quote: The CBB also equals the TAB unless there is a recognized Over-Target Baseline (OTB). In that case, the TAB equals the CBB plus Above Target Budget (ATB) (see Guideline 27).

statement: The DoD EVMS Interpretation Guide presents this requirement as its fourteenth guideline, on assessing progress.
quote: 4.1 GUIDELINE 14: ASSESS PROGRESS

statement: Using predefined performance measurement criteria, the contractor statuses the schedule and assesses physical progress to determine the budget earned.
quote: Using predefined performance measurement criteria, status the schedule and assess physical progress to determine budget earned.

statement: Earned value for material items may not be credited earlier than the actual receipt of the material nor later than the consumption of the item.
quote: Earned value for material items may not be credited earlier than the actual receipt of the material nor later than the consumption of the item.

statement: Schedule status and the physical progress assessment are updated in accordance with the business cycle based on the size, risk and complexity of the program, but no less than monthly.
quote: Schedule status (time-based) and assessing physical progress (earned value) is updated in accordance with the business cycle based on the size, risk, and complexity of the program, but no less than monthly.

statement: Level of effort performance is earned with the passage of time without consideration if actual work is performed.
quote: Level of Effort (LOE) performance is earned with the passage of time without consideration if actual work is performed.

statement: The point at which material costs transfer from the accounting system to the earned value system as actual cost must fall within the same accounting period in which earned value for that material is claimed.
quote: the point of transfer of costs from the accounting system to the Earned Value Management System (EVMS) as actual cost for the material occurs within the same accounting period that earned value for that material is claimed.

statement: To keep the schedule integrated with the baseline, the schedule progress reporting period should align to the accounting period.
quote: To ensure integration between the IMS and the Performance Measurement Baseline (PMB) the schedule progress reporting period should align to the accounting period.

statement: Guideline 15 requires actual direct and indirect costs to be collected by element of cost from a formal system controlled by the general books of account, for comparison with corresponding budgets.
quote: Collect actual costs (direct and indirect), by elements of cost, from a formal system controlled by the general books of account for comparison to corresponding budgets in the EVMS.

statement: When actual costs are not available for comparison, estimated costs are entered into the EVMS.
quote: Where actual costs are not available for comparison, estimated costs will be entered into the EVMS.

statement: Indirect costs must be allocated in a consistent manner to the contracts at the level where the indirect budgets are established.
quote: ensure all indirect costs are properly and correctly allocated in a consistent manner to the contract(s) at the level where indirect budgets are established.

statement: All purchased material for which earned value has been calculated must be accounted for, including material residual to the program.
quote: Account for all purchased material for which earned value has been calculated, including material residual to the program.

statement: The material management process must reflect acquisition, issue to control accounts, return of unused material, scrap quantity and disposition, and residual material inventory.
quote: This process must reflect the acquisition, issue to control accounts, return of unused materials from control accounts, scrap quantity and disposition, and residual material inventory.

statement: Schedule variance is the comparison of the amount of planned budget and the amount of budget earned for work accomplished.
quote: Comparison of the amount of planned budget and the amount of budget earned for work accomplished. This comparison provides the schedule variance.

statement: Cost variance is the comparison of the amount of the budget earned and the actual (applied where appropriate) direct costs for the same work.
quote: Comparison of the amount of the budget earned and the actual (applied where appropriate) direct costs for the same work. This comparison provides the cost variance.

statement: Schedule and cost variance information is generated at least monthly for the control account and higher levels, as necessary for management control, using actual cost data from or reconcilable with the accounting system.
quote: At least on a monthly basis, generate the following information for the control account and higher levels, as necessary for management control, using actual cost data from or reconcilable with the accounting system

statement: A positive schedule or cost variance value indicates a favorable condition, and a negative value indicates an unfavorable condition.
quote: A positive value indicates a favorable condition, and a negative value indicates an unfavorable condition.

statement: Guideline 18 requires identifying and evaluating, at least monthly for each control account, the significant differences between planned and actual schedule and cost performance, and analyzing and providing the reasons.
quote: Identify and evaluate, at least monthly for each control account, the significant differences between both planned and actual schedule performance and planned and actual cost performance; and analyze and provide the reasons for the variances in the detail needed by program management.

statement: Analyzing deviations from the performance measurement baseline lets management implement corrective actions to regain contract objectives.
quote: The ability to analyze deviations from the established Performance Measurement Baseline (PMB) permits management, at all levels, to implement corrective actions rapidly and effectively, to regain contract objectives.

statement: Schedule variance analysis is supplemented with integrated master schedule analysis and assesses the impact on future critical path, near-critical path, and driving path activities.
quote: Schedule variance analysis is supplemented with Integrated Master Schedule analysis and assesses the impact to future activities on the critical path, near-critical paths, and driving paths.

statement: Guideline 19 requires evaluating indirect cost variances and the impact of indirect cost performance on individual program performance.
quote: Evaluate indirect cost variances and the impact of indirect cost performance on individual program performance.

statement: The program's indirect cost variance is the portion of total cost variance attributed to indirect rate adjustments.
quote: The program’s indirect cost variance is the portion of the total cost variance attributed to indirect rate adjustments.

statement: Guideline 20 requires updating control account estimates at completion from variance analysis and indirect performance evaluations, and calculating the variance at completion by comparing to budgets.
quote: Using the results of control account variance analysis and indirect performance evaluations, update the control account estimates at completion to reflect future resource requirements to complete the remaining authorized work and, by comparing to budgets, calculate the variance at completion.

statement: The estimate at completion is the actual cost of work performed to date plus the estimate to complete for the remaining authorized work.
quote: The EAC is based on the Actual Cost of Work Performed (ACWP) to date plus the ETC for the remaining authorized work.

statement: Control account and summary level planning package estimates at completion are not constrained by funding, negotiated contract costs, or factored budgets.
quote: EACs are not constrained by funding, negotiated contract costs, or factored budgets (see Guideline 25).

statement: The variance at completion is the difference between the budget at completion and the estimate at completion for a control account or summary level planning package.
quote: Differences between the Budget at Completion (BAC) and EAC result in the CA and SLPP Variance at Completion (VAC).

statement: The variance at completion is calculated at least at the control account and summary level planning package levels.
quote: At a minimum, the VAC is calculated at the control account and SLPP levels.

statement: The guideline's purpose is to ensure that program performance status can be accurately summarized from the control account, at a minimum, through the work breakdown structure and organizational breakdown structure, for management insight and control and to meet customer reporting requirements.

statement: The data used for internal management control and for external customer reporting must be derived from the same data resident in the earned value management system.

statement: The guideline's purpose is to ensure that all levels of program management review performance measurement data, implement corrective action management plans, and use the information for decision making.

statement: The program's internal reports and the reports forwarded to the customer must indicate the overall cost and schedule impacts of program issues.

statement: At least annually, or more frequently if performance indicates the current estimate is invalid, a comprehensive or bottom-up estimate at completion is assessed at the contract level.

statement: The externally reported estimate at completion and the internal estimate at completion reconcile and have a clear, consistent relationship.

statement: When incorporating a customer directed change prior to negotiation, the work is planned based on the estimated value of the scope.

statement: Changes should never result in negative undistributed budget or management reserve values.

statement: Contract budget logs provide traceability of authorized baseline changes.

quote: Baseline changes within the freeze period are limited (e.g., customer-directed contract actions, rate changes, and economic price adjustments)

statement: Objective performance data tied to technical milestones provides management with accurate progress visibility and early indicators of program risks requiring corrective action.
